critical_code_review_comments: routers/youtube.py:143 — tags = (tags[:8] + ['QRU','education'])[:12] silently drops duplicates only within the first pass (via the `if t not in tags` check at line 141). If topic/title contains 'qru' or 'education' as words they will be duplicated in the final tag list. Guard the appended suffix tags with a de-dup check (`extra = [t for t in ['QRU','education'] if t.lower() not in {x.lower() for x in tags}]`).

routers/youtube.py:114 — _resolve_factory_asset queries db.media_assets.find_one WITHOUT excluding `_id`. The returned `factory_doc` is not serialized in the publish response body (only qru_asset_id is added), so nothing leaks — but for consistency with /factory-assets (which does exclude _id), pass projection={'_id':0} to avoid future serialization traps if the doc is ever returned directly.

routers/youtube.py:161 — GET /factory-assets uses `Depends(get_current_user)` (any authenticated user), while /publish requires super_admin. This is intentional (any user may browse Factory assets) but should be documented — the founder directive says 'publish directly', and a non-admin user seeing the list but being unable to publish is a UX-level 403 risk. Consider tightening to require_super_admin for consistency.

routers/youtube.py:222 — _extract_thumbnail writes JPG at `video_path + '.thumb.jpg'` (i.e., inside the vault directory). If the vault is read-only or backed by object storage in future deployments, this will fail silently (returns None → no thumbnail sent, honestly). Consider writing generated thumbnails to a temp dir (e.g., tempfile.NamedTemporaryFile) instead of the vault path so vault stays immutable.

YouTubePublisher.js:82 — publish() sets factory_asset_id: source === 'factory' ? factoryAssetId : null. Backend PublishInput accepts Optional[str] so `null` is fine, but the same call also sets video_upload_id from null in factory mode — for factory publishes the request body includes both `factory_asset_id` (real) and `video_upload_id: null`. Backend correctly branches on is_factory, but the body is slightly cluttered. Consider omitting null fields for cleanliness.

YouTubePublisher.js:62 — on mount, if factoryAssets fetch fails or returns empty (list.length===0), source is forced to 'manual'. This is correct behaviour, but for a channel with only draft-preview assets the user sees Manual mode by default and NO indicator that publishable Factory assets simply don't exist yet. Consider showing a hint above the toggle in that case.
